'''Fluentgrid Limited''' (formerly '''Phoenix IT Solutions Limited''') is an Indian enterprise software company headquartered in [[Visakhapatnam]], [[Andhra Pradesh]], that develops digital platforms for [[electricity]], [[water]] and [[gas]] utilities, as well as [[smart city]] and public infrastructure projects.<ref name="hindu2015">{{cite news
 |title=Phoenix IT Solutions rechristened Fluentgrid
 |work=The Hindu
 |date=22 December 2015
 |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Visakhapatnam/phoenix-it-solutions-rechristened-fluentgrid/article8016936.ece
 |access-date=16 July 2026
}}</ref> Founded on 4 December 1998 by Murali Krishna Gannamani, the company operated as Phoenix IT Solutions Limited until adopting its current name in December 2015.<ref name="hindu2015"/><ref name="care2026"/>

Its software has been deployed in utility and public-sector digital transformation projects, including the Integrated Command and Control Centre (ICCC) for the [[Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation]] (GVMC), a cloud-based customer billing platform for [[Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Limited]] (UPPCL), and COVID-19 response systems developed for the Visakhapatnam district administration in 2020.<ref name="juster2019">{{cite news
 |title=US envoy to India Kenneth Juster visits Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation command centre
 |work=The New Indian Express
 |date=16 November 2019
 |url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/states/andhra-pradesh/2019/nov/16/us-envoy-to-india-kenneth-juster-visits-greater-visakhapatnam-municipal-corporation-command-centre-2062440.html
 |access-date=16 July 2026
}}</ref><ref name="dcd2018">{{cite web
 |title=DCD Awards Asia Pacific 2018 winners announced
 |publisher=Data Center Dynamics (DCD)
 |date=12 September 2018
 |url=https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/event-news/dcdawards-asia-pacific-2018-winners-announced/
 |access-date=16 July 2026
}}</ref><ref name="hindu2020">{{cite news

 |access-date=16 July 2026
}}</ref>

The company has received industry recognition including the [[IBM]] Beacon Award (2012) and the Fierce Innovation Award for Energy (2015). Its software development organisation achieved [[Capability Maturity Model Integration]] (CMMI) Maturity Level 5 in 2017, and in 2025 Fluentgrid was recognised as a Major Player in the [[International Data Corporation]] (IDC) MarketScape assessment of worldwide utility meter data management system vendors.<ref name="ibm2012">{{cite web

== History ==

=== Foundation and early years (1998–2001) ===

Fluentgrid was founded on 4 December 1998 by Murali Krishna Gannamani in [[Visakhapatnam]] as Phoenix Cybertech (India) Private Limited, initially providing software and [[information technology]] services for [[electricity]] distribution utilities.<ref name="care2026"/><ref name="tofler">{{cite web
 |title=Fluentgrid Limited Financials
 |publisher=Tofler
 |url=https://www.tofler.in/fluentgrid-limited/company/U72200AP1998PLC030617
 |access-date=16 July 2026
}}</ref> In 2001, the company was converted into a public limited company and renamed Phoenix IT Solutions Limited.<ref name="care2026"/>

=== Rebranding and growth (2002–2015) ===

During the 2000s, the company expanded its software offerings for [[utility]] and infrastructure sectors.<ref name="care2026"/> In 2012, it received the [[IBM]] Beacon Award for Best Industry Solution for Energy and Utilities at the IBM PartnerWorld Leadership Conference.<ref name="ibm2012"/> On 16 December 2015, following approval from the [[Ministry of Corporate Affairs]], the company was renamed Fluentgrid Limited.<ref name="hindu2015"/> The rebranding reflected its focus on digital technologies for utilities and [[urban infrastructure]].<ref name="hindu2015"/> Later that year, it received the Fierce Innovation Award in the Energy category.<ref name="hindu2015award"/>

=== Recent developments (2016–present) ===

In 2016, Fluentgrid was recognised in the [[Deloitte]] Technology Fast 50 India programme and was subsequently included in the [[Deloitte Technology Fast 500]] Asia Pacific ranking.<ref name="deloitte50"/><ref name="deloitte500"/>

Its software development organisation achieved [[Capability Maturity Model Integration]] (CMMI) Maturity Level 5 in 2017.<ref name="prn2017cmmi"/> During the COVID-19 pandemic, the company developed digital systems to support testing, isolation management and emergency response for the Visakhapatnam district administration.<ref name="hindu2020"/>

In 2021, Fluentgrid became a participant in the [[United Nations Global Compact]].<ref name="ungc"/> In 2025, [[International Data Corporation]] (IDC) MarketScape named the company a Major Player in its worldwide utility [[meter data management]] systems vendor assessment.<ref name="idcmarketscape"/>

== Business overview ==

Fluentgrid develops enterprise software for [[electricity]], [[water]] and [[gas]] utilities, municipal authorities and other [[public sector]] infrastructure organisations.<ref name="care2026"/><ref name="infomerics2026">{{cite report
 |title=Fluentgrid Limited: Rating Rationale
 |publisher=Infomerics Valuation and Rating Pvt. Ltd.
 |date=18 March 2026
 |url=https://infomericstorage.blob.core.windows.net/uploads/pr_fluentgrid_18mar26_8d6c05beee.pdf
 |access-date=16 July 2026
}}</ref> Its software portfolio includes customer information and billing systems, [[smart metering]], [[meter data management]], outage management, [[enterprise asset management]] (EAM), and integrated command-and-control platforms for [[smart cities]], marketed under the brand name '''Actilligence'''.<ref name="care2026"/><ref name="actilligence2018">{{cite web
 |title=Actilligence for sustainable transformation of cities
 |publisher=Elets eGov
 |date=14 December 2018
 |url=https://egov.eletsonline.com/2018/12/actilligence-for-sustainable-transformation-of-cities/
 |access-date=17 July 2026
}}</ref>

The company's principal customers include [[electricity]] distribution utilities, [[municipal corporations]] and [[government agencies]] in India, together with projects in international markets.<ref name="care2026"/> Its business comprises [[software licensing]], [[systems integration]], [[managed services]], cloud-based deployments and annual maintenance contracts.<ref name="care2026"/><ref name="infomerics2026"/>

Fluentgrid is headquartered in [[Visakhapatnam]], Andhra Pradesh, where it operates its principal research and development centre. The company is part of the state's [[Economy of Andhra Pradesh|information technology industry]].<ref name="hindu2015"/><ref name="care2026"/> According to the company's corporate profile, its software has been deployed in more than 20 countries across over 50 [[utilities]] and [[cities]].<ref name="fgprofile">{{cite web
 |title=Fluentgrid Corporate Profile
 |publisher=Fluentgrid Limited
 |url=https://fluentgrid.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Fluentgrid-Profile.pdf
 |format=PDF
 |access-date=16 July 2026
}}</ref>

== Notable projects ==

Fluentgrid has implemented software platforms for utility and smart-city projects in India.

The company developed the Integrated Command and Control Centre (ICCC) for the [[Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation]], supporting city operations and emergency management. The facility was visited by then [[United States Ambassador to India]] [[Kenneth I. Juster]] during his official visit to [[Visakhapatnam]] in 2019.<ref name="juster2019"/>

For [[Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Limited (UPPCL)]], Fluentgrid implemented a [[cloud-based]] customer information and billing platform. The project was shortlisted in the Cloud Migration category at the Data Center Dynamics (DCD) Global Awards in 2018.<ref name="dcd2018"/>

Under the Government of India's [[Smart Cities Mission]], Lucknow Smart City Limited awarded a consortium of Fluentgrid and [[Bharat Electronics Limited]] the contract to implement the city's Integrated Command and Control Centre (ICCC), [[Geographic Information System]] (GIS) and citizen engagement platform.<ref name="lucknowchairman">{{cite web
 |title=The City of Culture on course to becoming truly 'Smart'
 |publisher=Elets eGov
 |date=7 December 2018
 |url=https://egov.eletsonline.com/2018/12/the-city-of-culture-on-course-to-becoming-truly-smart-anil-garg-chairman-lucknow-smart-city-limited/
 |access-date=17 July 2026
}}</ref><ref name="actilligence2018"/>

In 2019, a consortium comprising Fluentgrid and Bharat Electronics Limited was selected as the master system integrator for the Integrated Command, Control and Communication Centre (IC4) developed for Cochin Smart Mission Limited in Kochi, Kerala.<ref name="hindu2019kochi">{{cite news
 |title=Consortium selected to set up IC4 under Smart Mission
 |work=The Hindu
 |date=7 May 2019
 |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Kochi/consortium-selected-to-set-up-ic4-under-smart-mission/article27052521.ece
 |access-date=17 July 2026
}}</ref>

In 2021, Fluentgrid implemented a digital consumer electricity billing platform for Odisha Power Transmission Corporation Limited (OPTCL) as part of the utility's service modernisation programme.<ref name="odisha2021">{{cite news
 |title=Odisha: Digital electricity billing system launched for better services
 |work=The New Indian Express
 |date=3 October 2021
 |url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/states/odisha/2021/oct/03/odisha-digital-electricity-billing-system-launched-for-better-services-2367013.html
 |access-date=16 July 2026
}}</ref>

== Research and development ==

Fluentgrid operates an in-house [[research and development]] centre in [[Visakhapatnam]].<ref name="care2026"/> In 2017, its software development organisation was appraised at [[Capability Maturity Model Integration]] (CMMI) Maturity Level 5.<ref name="prn2017cmmi"/> The company's research and development centre is recognised by the [[Department of Scientific and Industrial Research]] (DSIR), [[Government of India]], as an in-house research and development unit.<ref name="dsirgov">{{cite web
 |title=Recognition of In-house R&D Units (RDI)
 |publisher=Department of Scientific and Industrial Research
 |url=https://s3d860edd1dd83b36f02ce52bde626c653.s3waas.gov.in/reconition-of-in-house-rd-units-rdi/
 |access-date=16 July 2026
}}</ref>

== Corporate affairs ==

=== Governance ===

Fluentgrid is a [[public company]] incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013, and is governed by a board of directors. The company files statutory and financial disclosures with India's [[Ministry of Corporate Affairs]].<ref name="tofler"/><ref name="care2026"/>

=== Leadership ===

Fluentgrid was founded by Murali Krishna Gannamani, who serves as its [[Managing Director]] and [[Chief Executive Officer]].<ref name="care2026"/> He served as Chairman of the [[Confederation of Indian Industry]] (CII), Andhra Pradesh, for the 2025–26 term, having previously chaired the organisation's [[Visakhapatnam]] Zone.<ref name="ciiap2025">{{cite news
 |title=CII Andhra Pradesh welcomes new leadership for 2025–26
 |work=Deccan Chronicle
 |date=20 March 2025
 |url=https://www.deccanchronicle.com/southern-states/andhra-pradesh/cii-andhra-pradesh-welcomes-new-leadership-for-202526-1868150
 |access-date=17 July 2026
}}</ref>

=== Memberships and community initiatives ===

Fluentgrid has participated in the [[United Nations Global Compact]] since 2021 and is a member of industry associations including the [[Confederation of Indian Industry]] (CII) and the India Smart Grid Forum (ISGF).<ref name="ungc"/><ref name="isgf">{{cite web
 |title=India Smart Grid Forum Members
 |publisher=India Smart Grid Forum
 |url=https://indiasmartgrid.org/
 |access-date=16 July 2026
}}</ref>

The company's [[corporate social responsibility]] initiatives are undertaken through the Ananda CitYzen Trust. Among its projects is a community-led smart neighbourhood programme in Kirlampudi Layout, [[Visakhapatnam]], developed in partnership with local residents.<ref name="toi2015kirlampudi">{{cite news

Founded on 4 December 1998 by Murali Krishna Gannamani, the company operated as Phoenix IT Solutions Limited until adopting its current name in December 2015.
Its software has been deployed in utility and public-sector digital transformation projects, including the Integrated Command and Control Centre (ICCC) for the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC), a cloud-based customer billing platform for Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Limited (UPPCL), and COVID-19 response systems developed for the Visakhapatnam district administration in 2020.
The company has received industry recognition including the IBM Beacon Award (2012) and the Fierce Innovation Award for Energy (2015). Its software development organisation achieved Capability Maturity Model Integration (CMMI) Maturity Level 5 in 2017, and in 2025 Fluentgrid was recognised as a Major Player in the International Data Corporation (IDC) MarketScape assessment of worldwide utility meter data management system vendors.
